secondGroup.description: With a `secondSplit`, a key of `margins.second`, `$other` and `$unknown` included: alone, that group's point of `margins.second`; with `group`, the cell of both, a series's `key` and `secondKey`. A point the result doesn't show is refused. Only with a `secondSplit`.

isPrevious.description: Whether the point is the comparison period's beside `bucketStart`, of `previousTotal` or a group's or cell's `previousValues`, its groups those the comparison period shows: the bucket at the same position for a `comparisonRange` and for `previous_period`, the one starting a year earlier for `previous_year`. The query needs a `comparison` or a `comparisonRange`. Defaults to false.

search.description: Only actors whose name, email, distinct id or key contains this, ignoring case; a group by its key or `name` property.

cursor.description: Where the page starts: the `pageInfo.endCursor` of the previous page. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: How many actors to return, from 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.

results.description: One result per query, in the order of the queries.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code money is in; null for counts.

unit.description: `money`, in integer minor units of the response's `currency`, or `count`.

buckets.description: The start of each bucket of the range; every series has a value per bucket.

total.description: The metric with the filters applied and no split, per bucket. Splits of money, counts, first times and sums add up to it; people, sessions and other statistics do not. With `isCumulative`, each bucket holds everything from the range's start through it.

previousTotal.description: `total` over the `comparison` period or the `comparisonRange`, bucket by bucket beside `buckets`; only with one of them. A year earlier, a bucket without a counterpart, such as 29 February, is null. Over a `comparisonRange` it holds every bucket of that range, so it is longer than `buckets` when the range is longer: draw the first `buckets.length` values and summarise them all.

key.description: The group's value, `$unknown` for rows without one, or `$other` for groups summed together: past the limit, or of fewer than five people.

label.description: A name for the key, such as a product's name; null when the key is its name.

values.description: The group's value per bucket, a number in every bucket: of a cell too, since a query split two ways withholds nothing.

previousValues.description: The group's values over the `comparison` period or the `comparisonRange`, measured by the same query with that period's own groups, lined up as `previousTotal` and as long as it; only with one of them. A group is matched by `key`, a cell of a `secondSplit` by `key` and `secondKey`, a margin's group by `key` within its dimension. Empty for a group that period did not show on its own, for `$other`, which sums different groups in each period, and for a cell with `$other` on either side.

secondKey.description: With a `secondSplit`, the cell's group of it, `$unknown` or `$other` as `key` is of `split`; `key` and `label` are then the cell's group of `split`. Only with a `secondSplit`.

secondLabel.description: A name for `secondKey`, such as a country's name; null when the key is its name. Only with a `secondSplit`.

series.description: One series per group of the split, biggest first; none without one. With a `secondSplit`, one per cell: each kept group of `split`, `$unknown` and `$other` included, with each kept group of `secondSplit`, ordered by the first group and then the second: the groups of `margins.first` by those of `margins.second`.

margins.description: Each dimension's own totals, only with a `secondSplit`, each the series a query split by that dimension alone returns. Money, counts, first times and sums of a row's cells add up to its `first` group, of a column's to its `second` group, and of each to `total`, in every bucket: no cell is withheld. People, sessions, groups and paying customers are counted for each group and cell itself, so they don't add up. A balance's groups add up as its cells do; its periods never do.

first.description: The metric per group of `split` alone, the same series a query split by `split` alone returns with the same `limit`.

second.description: The metric per group of `secondSplit` alone, the same series a query split by `secondSplit` alone returns with `secondLimit` as its limit.

isWithheld.description: Whether the values are withheld because a trait, the acquisition source or a group's property narrowed them to fewer than five people: `total` is null in every bucket and `series` is empty. Never with a `secondSplit`, which reads none of them.

hasOverlappingGroups.description: Whether one row can count in several groups of the split, as a person in two cohorts does, so the groups don't add up to `total`: shares of the total and stacked charts mean nothing. False without a split.

key.description: The group's value, `$unknown` for rows without one, or `$other` for groups summed together: past the limit, or of fewer than five people.

label.description: A name for the key, such as a product's name; null when the key is its name.

values.description: The group's value per bucket, a number in every bucket: of a cell too, since a query split two ways withholds nothing.

previousValues.description: The group's values over the `comparison` period or the `comparisonRange`, measured by the same query with that period's own groups, lined up as `previousTotal` and as long as it; only with one of them. A group is matched by `key`, a cell of a `secondSplit` by `key` and `secondKey`, a margin's group by `key` within its dimension. Empty for a group that period did not show on its own, for `$other`, which sums different groups in each period, and for a cell with `$other` on either side.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the organization's reporting currency, on monetary insights only.

value.description: The insight over the whole range: the last bucket for MRR, ARR, active subscriptions, active trials and persons; the change over the range for MRR growth rate; the average of the buckets for other rates; else the total. In the units of the sparkline.

basis.description: What a money insight counts of each charge: `gross`, `net_of_tax` or `proceeds`. Without it, `revenue`, `arpu`, `arppu` and `subscriber_lifetime_value` are gross, and `mrr`, `arr`, `mrr_growth_rate` and the MRR movements net of tax. Other insights ignore it.

filter.description: Narrows what the insight counts, such as to some stores, products or countries, or a store environment, keeping or leaving out values. `arpu` narrows its revenue, not the people active, who have no store, product or country until they buy; `subscriber_lifetime_value` narrows its revenue, paid subscriptions and churn alike. A field or operator the insight does not support fails with `unsupported_filter`.

insightId.description: The built-in insight. Money: `revenue` (purchases and renewals minus refunds), `mrr` (monthly recurring revenue, after tax and before the store's commission), `arr` (12 × MRR), `churned_revenue`, `new_mrr`, `expansion_mrr`, `contraction_mrr`, `reactivation_mrr`, `net_new_mrr`, `arpu`, `arppu` and `subscriber_lifetime_value`. Percentages: `mrr_growth_rate`, `churn_rate`, `retention`, `active_subscribers_growth` and `trial_conversion_rate`. Counts: `person_count`, `new_persons`, `active_subscriptions`, `active_trials`, `new_subscriptions`, `churned_subscriptions`, `trials` and `trial_conversions`.

field.description: The field compared: `store` (the store's provider id, such as `apple-app-store`), `product.id`, `country` (the store's storefront country, an ISO 3166 alpha-2 code such as `US`) and `provider.environment` (store environment: 1 production, 2 sandbox, 3 test) on revenue and subscription insights, `project.id` on every insight. A subscription insight narrows subscription by subscription: by its product at each change, so a subscription that moves to a product left out ends there, and by the storefront it was first charged in.

op.description: How `field` is compared with `value`. Insights support `eq` and `in` on every field, and `neq` and `not_in` on every field but `provider.environment`, to leave values out; another operator fails with `unsupported_filter`. Filters on different fields combine with `and`; `or` joins values to keep of one field, and `not` wraps one comparison.
